items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: I said, 'Well, man I am Wilbur Ware.' ... and do you know that I stayed with that cat; that cat would not let me out of his sight.

ctx.x: But I remember that period -- I'm going back -- this is 1933, just before Reverend Turner made that fiddle for me. The Vendome (phonetic) Theatre was still open, and Erskine Tate had a band in there, they used to have amateur shows -- and I wanted to get on that show so bad. I made it -- dancing. I didn't win anything cause I wasn't good enough, but the music, oh, I was crazy when I hit that stage. I don't know what routine I had; I forgot -- but the music was so beautiful.

Then another time, there was the Grand Theatre on the corner of 31st and State, and the Vendome was in the 31st block on State, and there was a little theatre called the Lincoln Theatre, and they would bring in stage shows. I remember my first movie -- of course Reverend Turner didn't know I was going. I went in, they had a stage show -- a vaudeville show -- and the movie was "City Lights" and the first talkie. Goodness, yes. The first talkie with Tom Tyler in some cowboy picture.
And I had never been to the movies; I didn't know -- nobody told me when to come out. I think I went in about 2 o'clock, and I stepped out of the show when it closed.
